newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: First Austrian says may rejoin group bid for CA.
newsitem.headline: First Austrian says may rejoin group bid for CA.

text.p: First Austrian bank said on Monday there was a strong possibility it would rejoin an international consortium bidding for a stake in flagship bank Creditanstalt Bankverein, two months after quitting the group.
"The decision-making process is still going on...(but) the chances of a joint bid with the EA-Generali group are very good," supervisory board president Herbert Schimetschek told journalists.
Die Erste Oesterreichische SparCasse Bank AG (First Austrian) split with the EA-Generali consortium on September 6 following a disagreement over the form their bid should take.
"If there is another bid it should be higher than the previous one," Schimetschek said.

The EA-Generali group, which also includes Germany's Commerzbank and Italy's Banca Commerciale Italiana, in September bid around 6.7 billion schillings ($629.3 million) for roughly half the state's 19.9 million ordinary shares.
But the finance ministry rejected the offer and restarted the sale, now in its seventh year.
The latest tender for the government's 70 percent voting stake closes on November 15. Finance Minister Viktor Klima has said he expects more than one offer to land on his desk by the deadline.
A host of suitors has come and gone since 1991 when the government first put Creditanstalt at the top of its privatisation list.
Several international bidders dropped their interest amid allegations they faced discrimination during the due diligence process because of Austrian opposition to foreign ownership.
Klima has said he expects the sale of the government's 19.9 million shares in the bank to be wrapped up before year-end. At current market value, the stake is worth about 14.5 billion schillings.
-- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 254 ($ = 10.64 Austrian Schillings)
